subject: Regional switchover exception request — proposed bounded RTO/RPO
messages:

Cc: Samantha Price <samantha.price@finsecure.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: RTO/RPO expectations for multi-region switchover

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the demo last week — the latency numbers looked good. Before we proceed to procurement we need clarity on the operational guarantees for cross-region failover. Our compliance team wants a written commitment that, in the event of a primary region outage, the switchover to the standby region will meet an RTO <= 10 minutes and RPO <= 5 minutes for our production traffic.

Can Redwood commit to those numbers for our account (FinSecure) in the US regions? If not, what carving/scope changes can we accept to get close? We also need to understand implications for retention of audit logs and whether there will be any temporary reduction in throughput during failover.

Appreciate a concise summary (and any proposed contract language) that we can route to our legal/compliance.

Thanks,
Matt
Director of SRE — FinSecure

Subject: Re: RTO/RPO expectations for multi-region switchover

Hi Matt — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: our standard multi-region failover SLO for hosted customers targets RTO <= 30 minutes and RPO <= 10 minutes. Hitting RTO <= 10m / RPO <= 5m is possible for a scoped set of customers under a bounded exception if we apply the following constraints:

- Dedicated standby capacity reserved for FinSecure (pre-warmed GPUs in the standby region).
- Synchronous state replication for critical KV caches (adds cost and operational risk).
- Pre-established traffic-split and DNS TTL lowering during the contractually-defined maintenance window.
- Limited model profile: to guarantee 10m/5m we must cap peak concurrent streams per-customer and restrict longest-context models.

I’ve looped in Marissa (SRE) for operational details and Neha (legal) for suggested contract language. If FinSecure is open to the commercial and operational trade-offs (dedicated reserve + monthly standby fee), we can draft an addendum that enumerates the exact failover steps, traffic shaping, and temporary throughput knobs during the switchover.

Proposed next step: Marissa to propose a runbook + capacity matrix; Neha to propose exception wording. If helpful, we can also outline a mutual action plan and a short on-call rehearsal schedule.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: RTO/RPO expectations for multi-region switchover

Matt / Jasmine — operational notes from SRE perspective. I attached a first-pass capacity matrix and an ops runbook stub (see attachments). Key items: 

1) Timeline and steps (high level):
   - Detection & decision (0-1m): automated health checks + manual confirm (we recommend 2FA confirm for production switchover).
   - Traffic cutover (1-6m): lower DNS TTL, update routing, begin connection draining in primary. 3rd-party CDN propagation still a variable.
   - KV sync validation & cache warm (6-10m): our continuous prefix caching reduces load but full warm requires ongoing background fetches.
   - Throughput steady-state (10-30m): once caches are warm and autoscaling finishes, throughput should return to baseline.

2) Failure modes we cannot absolutely eliminate: long-tail cold caches (impacts RPO on in-flight sessions), third-party upstreams failing to reconnect, and model loading for very large weights which can add minutes.

3) Mitigations to reach 10m/5m target: dedicated preloaded model shards in standby, synchronous replication for critical KV namespaces, and a reduced-model-profile during switchover. All require reserved capacity and an operational playbook.

4) Audit logs: we can guarantee audit-log continuity (writes replicated asynchronously) but write durability semantics differ — we can include a clause that log commits are preserved with a max delay of 30s post-failover.

I recommend a scoped pilot: 2-week pre-warm window, one scheduled rehearsal switchover, followed by a live-failover SLA amendment if the rehearsal meets the targets.

Attachments: DR-ops-runbook_v1.pdf, regional-capacity-matrix.xlsx

—Marissa
Senior SRE — Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: RTO/RPO expectations for multi-region switchover — proposed addendum language

Hi all,

Draft wording for the addendum (high-level) below. This is intentionally restrictive to limit commercial exposure: 

1) Scope: The regional failover exceptions apply only to traffic originating from FinSecure production namespaces identified in Appendix A. The exception is limited to the US West and US East regions and does not apply to other global regions.

2) Commitment: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to achieve an RTO not exceeding ten (10) minutes and an RPO not exceeding five (5) minutes for the Scope set forth in Section 1, provided that Customer accepts the Operational Constraints in Section 3.

3) Operational Constraints: Customer agrees to (a) purchase Reserved Standby Capacity as described in Exhibit B; (b) accept a reduced model profile during switchover as described in Exhibit C; and (c) participate in quarterly switchover rehearsals.

4) Remedies: If Redwood fails to meet the RTO/RPO in a declared failover for two (2) or more events in a rolling 12-month period, Customer is entitled to service credits capped at the Reserved Standby Capacity monthly fee.

5) Limitations & Force Majeure: Standard carve-outs for third-party upstreams, DNS propagation, and material network partitioning apply; these events will not be counted as Redwood performance failures.

I’ll prepare a redline version for legal review. Aditya — can you confirm the commercial numbers we discussed (monthly standby fee + rehearsal credits)?

Neha Kapoor
Head of Legal — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Regional switchover exception request — commercial proposal and MAP

Matt — quick commercial summary and proposed mutual action plan (MAP):

- Reserved Standby Capacity: $18,000/month (dedicated GPU pool sized for FinSecure peak, incl. 1 pre-warm cycle per month).
- Rehearsal program: two scheduled rehearsals in the first 90 days (no charge), quarterly thereafter (discounted rate or credit if Redwood cancels due to internal reasons).
- SLA addendum term: 12 month minimum to cover capacity reservation.
- Credits: if we miss the agreed RTO/RPO per Neha’s draft, credits capped at one month of the Reserved Standby fee per rolling 12-month period.

Proposed MAP:
1) Finalize Appendix A (namespace list) — FinSecure target: by 2026-09-24.
2) Redwood to deliver runbook + capacity matrix — Marissa by 2026-09-18 (attached).
3) Legal to circulate redline addendum — Neha by 2026-09-20.
4) Signage + Standby provisioning — upon signature, 7-10 business days to provision.

If Matt and Samantha confirm acceptance of the MAP and the pricing, I’ll generate the DocuSign and we can kick off provisioning and the first rehearsal.

Thanks — Aditya
